summary:
Vita Lunae is an interactive educational survival game designed for children aged 7 to 12, developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Players manage a lunar base, complete missions, solve puzzles, and balance essential resources such as oxygen, energy, and crew health. Every decision has consequences that influence future challenges and lead to different endings, while adaptive difficulty ensures an engaging experience for players of different skill levels.

The game incorporates real scientific data from NASA, including space weather information from DONKI and space biology research from OSDR, to provide an educational experience grounded in science. Players are accompanied by Kita, a friendly virtual assistant who answers questions, offers hints, and explains scientific concepts in simple language. By combining exploration, problem-solving, and interactive challenges, Vita Lunae encourages children to think critically, learn from their mistakes, and understand the importance of managing limited resources. Beyond entertainment, the project aims to spark curiosity about science and inspire young minds to explore the possibilities of space. Through this experience, Vita Lunae shows that even the smallest choices can have a significant impact, teaching players one essential lesson: in space, every decision matters.
details:
What it does. VITA LUNAE is an educational 2D pixel-art survival game that transforms lunar science into an interactive adventure. Players become astronauts responsible for surviving on the Moon, managing limited resources, and overcoming challenges inspired by real space exploration.

Guided by Kita, a friendly alien companion, players discover scientific concepts through exploration, problem-solving, and meaningful decisions.

Our goal is simple: make space science accessible, engaging, and memorable through gameplay.
How it works. Players explore a lunar base centered around Zora, their spacecraft, and complete 50 interconnected challenges involving:

  • Life support: Managing oxygen, health, and essential survival systems.
  • Energy management: Maintaining solar panels, batteries, and electrical systems.
  • Food production: Growing crops and managing water and nutrients inside a lunar greenhouse.
  • Communication systems: Repairing equipment and maintaining contact with Earth.
  • Lunar exploration: Investigating craters, collecting samples, and managing environmental hazards.
  • Radiation protection: Making decisions to reduce exposure to dangerous space radiation.

Every decision matters. Failing one mission can affect future challenges, available resources, and even the player's survival.

The game incorporates adaptive difficulty, multiple endings, and LUNI, an in-game currency used to purchase equipment and supplies.

Learning by design. Instead of traditional quizzes or memorization, VITA LUNAE integrates scientific knowledge directly into gameplay.

Players face situations inspired by lunar conditions, applying critical thinking to manage resources, solve emergencies, and understand the consequences of their actions.

NASA scientific resources help connect these challenges to real space exploration. Even failure becomes an opportunity to learn.

Benefits and impact. VITA LUNAE makes space science more approachable through an experience that combines education and entertainment.

Designed for students, young gamers, educators, and space enthusiasts, the game encourages scientific curiosity, problem-solving, and strategic thinking.

Our proposal goes beyond teaching scientific facts: it allows players to experience why those facts matter.
Tools and technologies.

  • Visual design: Original 2D pixel-art environments, SVG assets, character animations, and interactive maps.
  • Game systems: Resource management, adaptive difficulty, interconnected missions, and consequence-based storytelling.
  • Scientific foundation: NASA educational resources and scientific data related to lunar exploration.
  • Development: Frontend and backend integration, character customization, inventory, and game-state management.

Creativity. VITA LUNAE combines a charming pixel-art world with realistic survival challenges.

Players explore Zora, a greenhouse, solar installations, and lunar craters while interacting with Kita, their animated companion.

Unlike conventional educational games, VITA LUNAE connects decisions across missions, allowing players to experience different outcomes and endings depending on their actions.

Factors we considered

  • Inclusivity and accessibility: Color-based challenges include recognizable symbols for players with color vision deficiencies, reducing reliance on color alone.
  • Character customization: Players can personalize their astronauts, encouraging self-expression and a stronger connection with the experience.
  • Adaptive difficulty: Challenges accommodate different skill levels, making the game approachable for beginners.
  • Scientific accuracy: Missions are inspired by real lunar conditions and NASA scientific resources.
  • Engagement: Exploration, rewards, meaningful consequences, and multiple endings make learning interactive and enjoyable.

We aim to avoid creating educational games that exclude players or reduce learning to repetitive questions. Instead, we prioritize accessibility, creativity, and learning through experience.

We don't just teach players how astronauts survive on the Moon. We let them discover what it takes to survive, because everyone can be an astronaut.
